description: Soy un adolescente inquieto y muy creativo que disfruta de explorar nuevas experiencias. Busco compañeros para armar un equipo de trabajo que sean buenos en dibujar, crear maquetas y contar historias.
summary: We developed the project titled "An Unexpected Trip to the Moon," a narrative and visual resource composed of a comic-style illustrated storybook and a physical model with elements built out of LEGO, animated through coding in Canva Code, starring three kids: Ian, Leo, and Sebas. The project addresses the challenge of bringing complex concepts of aerospace history and lunar engineering closer to children by transforming real historical artifacts—such as the descent stage of the Apollo Lunar Module, the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), and the ALSEP scientific package—into friendly characters that explain how they work within an adventure. This project is important because it sparks curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and space exploration from an early age, making scientific concepts easier to understand through play, imagination, and storytelling. It is a story made by kids, for kids.
details:
• What does it do exactly? It narrates and illustrates an educational story titled "An Unexpected Trip to the Moon," presented both as a physical model and as a comic strip. Through the adventures of three kids—Ian, Leo, and Sebas—who accidentally travel into space, the project interactively and visually introduces and explains the real-life functions of three historical artifacts from the Apollo missions: the descent stage of the Lunar Module, the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), and the ALSEP scientific package. 
  • How does it work? It works through personification and visual storytelling. Instead of presenting technical data in a traditional way, the story turns space equipment into friendly characters that converse with the protagonists on the lunar surface and explain in the first person how they helped astronauts land, travel across craters, and collect scientific data on the Moon. The concept involves an interactive app featuring a multi-language audio player (using browser speech synthesis), a progress bar, playback speed controls, synchronized word-by-word highlighted reading by chapters, and a gallery of upcoming stories. It also includes interactive collectible cards for Ian, Leo, Sebas, the Apollo Descent Module, the LRV Rover, and the ALSEP Package with signature catchphrases and real NASA scientific facts, alongside themed educational capsules, a 4-question interactive quiz to unlock space badges, and direct links to official portals such as NASA Space Place in Spanish and NASA Kids' Club. 
    • Educational accessibility: It presents complex aerospace history and engineering concepts in clear, fun, and understandable language so young audiences fall in love with science. 
    • Visual and emotional learning: By combining narrative, humor, and illustrated comic panels, it improves information retention and keeps children engaged. 
    • Format versatility: Having both the illustrated text and the comic version makes it widely adaptable as classroom reading material, a digital resource, or a printed book. 
  • What do you hope to achieve? To spark scientific curiosity and foster early interest in STEM fields (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) among boys and girls, demonstrating that the history of space exploration is exciting and accessible to everyone regardless of age. 
  • What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? We used a double motor, a controller and a color sensor from LEGO Education Computer Science & AI. Software Platform: Coding Canvas from LEGO Education Computer Science & AI.
